stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amidst defense demand
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. This funding reflects growing interest in co-orbital security and space domain awareness, with the Department of Defense playing an increasingly pivotal role. Investors are clearly betting that space security will be a lucrative market.
stories.soWhat: If you thought the space race was just about exploration, think again—it's a defense play now.

stories.head: SpaceX tests Starship 13, fixes and all
stories.body: SpaceX's 13th Starship test flight included some fixes and the debut of functioning satellites, demonstrating the company's relentless pursuit of launch frequency. Despite the ongoing challenges, each test brings them closer to operational readiness, though the timeline remains as flexible as their launch windows.
stories.soWhat: SpaceX is proving that in aerospace, failure is just a pit stop on the way to the next launch.

stories.head: Commerce Department advances mission authorization system
stories.body: The Office of Space Commerce is moving forward with a voluntary mission authorization system for novel space activities, a step that could streamline regulatory hurdles but also introduces a layer of ambiguity. This initiative could reshape how companies approach compliance, especially as space activities proliferate.
stories.soWhat: When regulations start to sound like a choose-your-own-adventure book, expect a wild ride for operators.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on SpaceX's next launch
watchlist.body: With the 14th test flight on the horizon, expect more updates on their operational timeline.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension implications
watchlist.body: The $480 million extension could signal increased government reliance on tech for defense capabilities.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris partnership developments

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
